Now I can see the issue clearly. The application loads shards into memory before opening its HTTP listener at port 8080. There's a new index snapshot as of today (catalog-2026-05-12T03) with 48 shards (12.4 GiB). The application takes about ~50+ seconds to load all shards, but the liveness probe starts checking at 30 seconds after start (`delay=30s`). 

The liveness probe has: `delay=30s timeout=1s period=10s #failure=3` - so it starts at 30s, then checks every 10s. With 3 failures, the probe will fail and kill the container at approximately 30 + 10 + 10 = 50 seconds (after 3 consecutive failures). 

Since each shard takes roughly 2-3 seconds to load and the HTTP listener only opens once all 48 are loaded, the full startup would take somewhere around 100-140 seconds — but the liveness probe is killing the container well before that, around the 50 second mark, so it never gets the chance to finish loading and start serving traffic.

The fix is either bumping up the liveness probe's initialDelaySeconds to cover the full shard-loading time, or switching to a startupProbe designed for exactly this situation. Let me check the docs to compare startup probes against liveness probes for this use case.
